issue.title: Prompt $EDITOR temp file is deleted when the editor exits non-zero, losing everything typed there

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone who edits a prompt in $EDITOR and exits non-zero loses everything typed in that editor session with no warning. This defeats the "never lose a user prompt" guarantee that epic sase-1ca delivered for the stash, restore, capture, and quit paths.
task_type_fields.repro:
`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_editor.py` (`_open_editor_for_prompt` → `run_editor`, lines ~41-78; the workflow-YAML editor at ~118-138 has the same shape) writes the draft to a `mkstemp` file, runs `$EDITOR`, and on `result.returncode != 0` returns `None`, and the `finally` block then unconditionally `os.unlink(temp_path)`.

Repro: open a prompt in ACE, press the open-in-editor key, type a long prompt in nvim, then exit with `:cq` (or let the editor crash / get killed). The temp file holding everything typed in the editor is deleted and the TUI treats it as a cancel. Nothing is stashed or archived.

Fix direction (listed as a follow-up candidate in the approved sase-1ca plan, "Never lose stashed prompts"): on a non-zero exit, keep the temp file when its content differs from the initial content, and toast its path (or stash it with a recovery source). Unlink only on success or when nothing changed.

issue.creation_reason: The approved sase-1ca plan listed this as an out-of-scope follow-up; the sase-1ca land agent confirmed the unconditional unlink in _editor.py while routing follow-ups.
